name: Transparency and Openness Promotion (TOP) Guidelines
authority: Center for Open Science / Nosek et al., Science (2015)

standards.name: Citation Standards
standards.description: All data, code, software packages, and materials are formally cited with persistent identifiers (DOIs, RRIDs, or accession numbers) in the reference list.

standards.name: Data Transparency
standards.description: Raw and processed data files are deposited in a trusted, public, permanent repository (e.g., OSF, Zenodo, Dataverse, GitHub Release) with verified open access.

standards.name: Analytic Methods (Code) Transparency
standards.description: Complete source code, scripts, and software environments required to reproduce all tables, figures, and statistical tests are deposited and documented.

standards.name: Research Materials Transparency
standards.description: Complete experimental materials (survey instruments, stimulus texts, hardware setups, formal verification files) are fully accessible.

standards.name: Design and Analysis Transparency
standards.description: Adheres to domain-specific reporting guidelines; explicitly documents participant exclusions, attrition, sample size determination, and randomization.

standards.name: Study Preregistration
standards.description: The study design, primary hypotheses, and experimental protocols were formally pre-registered in an independent public registry prior to data collection.

standards.name: Analysis Plan Preregistration
standards.description: The statistical analysis plan, primary endpoints, and data exclusion rules were pre-registered and frozen, distinguishing confirmatory from exploratory tests.

standards.name: Replication & Computational Verification
standards.description: The paper provides an independent empirical replication or automated continuous-integration verification suite verifying bit-exact reproduction.
